metadata.name: CIS Benchmark for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 - Level 2 Server
metadata.description: Center for Internet Security Benchmark for RHEL 9 Level 2 Server Profile - Extended security controls
metadata.author: Center for Internet Security

profile.name: CIS Level 2 Server
profile.description: Enhanced security configuration for RHEL 9 servers - Level 2 includes all Level 1 controls plus additional hardening

rules.rule_name: Ensure mounting of cramfs filesystems is disabled
rules.rule_description: Level 2: The cramfs filesystem type is a compressed read-only Linux filesystem embedded in small footprint systems. Disabling unnecessary filesystem types reduces the attack surface.

assessment.detection_step: Verify cramfs kernel module is disabled

remediation.remediation_step: Create or edit /etc/modprobe.d/cramfs.conf with: install cramfs /bin/true

context.rationale: Unused filesystem drivers increase attack surface and should be disabled.

rules.rule_name: Ensure /var/log is a separate partition
rules.rule_description: Level 2: The /var/log directory should be on a separate partition to prevent log flooding from affecting the root filesystem.

remediation.remediation_step: Create separate partition for /var/log and migrate data

context.rationale: Separate log partition prevents disk exhaustion from affecting system operation.

rules.rule_name: Ensure /var/log/audit is a separate partition
rules.rule_description: Level 2: The audit logs should be on a separate partition to ensure audit trail integrity.

remediation.remediation_step: Create separate partition for /var/log/audit and configure in /etc/fstab

context.rationale: Separate audit partition ensures audit logs cannot fill the root filesystem.

rules.rule_name: Ensure /home is a separate partition
rules.rule_description: Level 2: The /home directory should be on a separate partition.

remediation.remediation_step: Create separate partition for /home with nodev,nosuid options

context.rationale: Separate home partition allows disk quotas and restrictive mount options.

rules.rule_name: Ensure filesystem integrity is regularly checked
rules.rule_description: Level 2: AIDE should be configured to run regular file integrity checks via cron.

assessment.detection_step: Verify AIDE cron job is configured
assessment.expected_value: AIDE check cron entry should be present

context.rationale: Regular integrity checks detect unauthorized file changes.

rules.rule_name: Ensure message of the day is configured properly
rules.rule_description: Level 2: The MOTD should be configured with appropriate security warnings.

remediation.remediation_step: Configure /etc/motd with authorized access warning banner

context.rationale: Warning banners support legal prosecution of unauthorized access.

rules.rule_name: Ensure local login warning banner is configured properly
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Local login banner should display appropriate security warnings.

context.rationale: Login banners establish authorization requirements.

rules.rule_name: Ensure remote login warning banner is configured properly
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Remote login (SSH) banner should display appropriate security warnings.

context.rationale: SSH banners establish authorization requirements for remote access.

rules.rule_name: Ensure permissions on /etc/motd are configured
rules.rule_description: Level 2: The MOTD file must have proper permissions to prevent unauthorized modification.

context.rationale: Protects banner content from unauthorized modification.

rules.rule_name: Ensure permissions on /etc/issue are configured
rules.rule_description: Level 2: The issue file must have proper permissions.

context.rationale: Protects banner content from unauthorized modification.

rules.rule_name: Ensure GNOME Display Manager is removed
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Graphical display managers should not be installed on servers.

context.rationale: GUI packages increase attack surface and are unnecessary on servers.

rules.rule_name: Ensure X Window System is not installed
rules.rule_description: Level 2: X Window System should not be installed on servers.

assessment.detection_step: Verify X11 packages are not installed

remediation.remediation_step: Remove X11 packages: dnf groupremove 'X Window System'

context.rationale: X11 increases attack surface and resource usage.

rules.rule_name: Ensure auditd is installed
rules.rule_description: Level 2: The audit daemon must be installed for security auditing.

context.rationale: Audit daemon is essential for security monitoring and compliance.

rules.rule_name: Ensure auditd service is enabled and running
rules.rule_description: Level 2: The audit daemon must be enabled and running.

assessment.check_command: systemctl is-enabled auditd && systemctl is-active auditd

remediation.remediation_step: Enable and start auditd: systemctl enable --now auditd

context.rationale: Running auditd is essential for security event logging.

rules.rule_name: Ensure audit log storage size is configured
rules.rule_description: Level 2: The maximum size of audit log files should be configured.

context.rationale: Adequate log size ensures sufficient audit trail retention.

rules.rule_name: Ensure audit logs are not automatically deleted
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Audit logs should be retained rather than automatically deleted.

context.rationale: Retaining logs supports forensic analysis and compliance.

rules.rule_name: Ensure events that modify date/time information are collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor for changes to system time.

assessment.expected_value: Audit rules for time modification present

context.rationale: Time changes can be used to hide malicious activity.

rules.rule_name: Ensure events that modify user/group information are collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor for changes to user and group information.

assessment.expected_value: Audit rules for identity files present

context.rationale: User/group changes are critical security events.

rules.rule_name: Ensure events that modify the system's network environment are collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor for changes to network configuration.

assessment.expected_value: Audit rules for network environment present

context.rationale: Network configuration changes may indicate compromise.

rules.rule_name: Ensure events that modify the system's mandatory access controls are collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor for changes to SELinux configuration.

assessment.expected_value: Audit rules for SELinux changes present

context.rationale: SELinux changes are critical security events.

rules.rule_name: Ensure login and logout events are collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor login and logout events.

assessment.expected_value: Audit rules for login events present

context.rationale: Login monitoring is essential for security analysis.

rules.rule_name: Ensure session initiation information is collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor session initiation events.

assessment.expected_value: Audit rules for session tracking present

context.rationale: Session tracking supports security analysis.

rules.rule_name: Ensure discretionary access control permission modification events are collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor file permission changes.

assessment.expected_value: Audit rules for permission changes present

context.rationale: Permission changes are critical security events.

rules.rule_name: Ensure unsuccessful unauthorized file access attempts are collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor failed file access attempts.

assessment.expected_value: Audit rules for unauthorized access present

context.rationale: Failed access attempts may indicate reconnaissance.

rules.rule_name: Ensure use of privileged commands is collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor privileged command execution.

assessment.expected_value: Audit rules for privileged commands present

remediation.remediation_step: Add audit rules for all setuid/setgid binaries

context.rationale: Privileged command monitoring is essential for security.

rules.rule_name: Ensure successful file system mounts are collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor filesystem mount events.

assessment.expected_value: Audit rules for mount events present

context.rationale: Mount events may indicate unauthorized filesystem access.

rules.rule_name: Ensure file deletion events by users are collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor file deletion events.

assessment.expected_value: Audit rules for deletion events present

context.rationale: File deletion may indicate evidence destruction.

rules.rule_name: Ensure changes to system administration scope are collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor sudoers changes.

context.rationale: Sudoers changes affect administrative access.

rules.rule_name: Ensure system administrator actions are collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor system administrator command execution.

assessment.expected_value: Audit rules for admin actions present

context.rationale: Admin action monitoring supports accountability.

rules.rule_name: Ensure kernel module loading/unloading and modification is collected
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Monitor kernel module changes.

assessment.expected_value: Audit rules for module changes present

context.rationale: Kernel module changes may indicate rootkit installation.

rules.rule_name: Ensure the audit configuration is immutable
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Audit configuration should be immutable to prevent tampering.

context.rationale: Immutable audit rules prevent tampering with audit configuration.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SSH approved ciphers are used
rules.rule_description: Level 2: SSH should only use approved ciphers.

assessment.expected_value: Only strong ciphers listed (aes256-ctr, aes192-ctr, aes128-ctr)

context.rationale: Weak ciphers can be exploited to decrypt SSH traffic.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SSH approved MAC algorithms are used
rules.rule_description: Level 2: SSH should only use approved MAC algorithms.

context.rationale: Weak MAC algorithms can be exploited.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SSH approved kex algorithms are used
rules.rule_description: Level 2: SSH should only use approved key exchange algorithms.

context.rationale: Weak key exchange algorithms can be exploited.

rules.rule_name: Ensure lockout for failed password attempts is configured
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Accounts should be locked after multiple failed login attempts.

assessment.expected_value: pam_faillock configured with deny and unlock_time

remediation.service_impact: Accounts may be locked after failed attempts

context.rationale: Account lockout mitigates brute force attacks.

rules.rule_name: Ensure password reuse is limited
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Password reuse should be limited.

context.rationale: Password history prevents password cycling.

rules.rule_name: Ensure system accounts are secured
rules.rule_description: Level 2: System accounts should be properly secured.

assessment.detection_step: Verify system accounts are locked or nologin
assessment.expected_value: System accounts should have /sbin/nologin or /bin/false shell

remediation.remediation_step: Lock system accounts and set nologin shell: usermod -L -s /sbin/nologin <account>

context.rationale: System accounts should not allow interactive login.

rules.rule_name: Ensure default group for the root account is GID 0
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Root's primary group should be GID 0 (root).

context.rationale: Root should have consistent group membership.

rules.rule_name: Ensure default user umask is 027 or more restrictive
rules.rule_description: Level 2: Default umask should be restrictive.

context.rationale: Restrictive umask prevents world-readable files by default.

rules.rule_name: Ensure no world-writable files exist
rules.rule_description: Level 2: No files should be world-writable.

assessment.check_command: df --local -P | awk '{if (NR!=1) print $6}' | xargs -I '{}' find '{}' -xdev -type f -perm -0002

context.rationale: World-writable files allow any user to modify them.

rules.rule_name: Ensure no unowned files or directories exist
rules.rule_description: Level 2: All files should have a valid owner.

remediation.remediation_step: Assign owner to unowned files: chown root <file> or remove

context.rationale: Unowned files may be exploited if a user is assigned that UID.

rules.rule_name: Ensure no ungrouped files or directories exist
rules.rule_description: Level 2: All files should have a valid group.

remediation.remediation_step: Assign group to ungrouped files: chgrp root <file> or remove

context.rationale: Ungrouped files may be exploited if a group is assigned that GID.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SUID executables are reviewed
rules.rule_description: Level 2: All SUID executables should be reviewed for necessity.

assessment.check_command: df --local -P | awk '{if (NR!=1) print $6}' | xargs -I '{}' find '{}' -xdev -type f -perm -4000

remediation.remediation_step: Remove SUID bit from unnecessary binaries: chmod -s <file>

context.rationale: SUID binaries can be exploited for privilege escalation.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SGID executables are reviewed
rules.rule_description: Level 2: All SGID executables should be reviewed for necessity.

assessment.check_command: df --local -P | awk '{if (NR!=1) print $6}' | xargs -I '{}' find '{}' -xdev -type f -perm -2000

remediation.remediation_step: Remove SGID bit from unnecessary binaries: chmod -s <file>

context.rationale: SGID binaries can be exploited for privilege escalation.
